common_name: Dwarf Sweet Sue Tomato (Golden-Yellow Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit with thick, sturdy stems suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking lightly since the sturdy, potato-leaf stems need less support than sprawling indeterminate types. Dwarf Sweet Sue bears round to oblate golden-yellow fruit, often blushed pink at the blossom end when fully ripe, with a rich, well-balanced, notably sweet flavor for a yellow tomato. It was bred from a 2005 cross of Golden Dwarf Champion and Green Giant by Patrina Nuske Small and named by Craig LeHoullier for his wife, one of the earlier stabilized releases of the international Dwarf Tomato Project. Harvest as fruit colors fully and softens slightly for peak sweetness.

common_name: Dwarf Kelly Green Tomato (Green-Fleshed Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit with thick stems suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking lightly since the thick, rugose-leafed stems need less support than sprawling indeterminate types. Dwarf Kelly Green bears medium, round fruit that stays green with a translucent amber-tinged skin even at full ripeness, offering the tangy, well-rounded flavor typical of green-fleshed tomatoes. It came from the same 2005 Golden Dwarf Champion x Green Giant cross that produced Dwarf Sweet Sue, stabilized through the Dwarf Tomato Project and named for Australian bushranger Ned Kelly. Harvest when fruit softens slightly, since color alone will not signal ripeness.

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit, taller than most dwarfs, still benefits from container or raised-bed growing with light staking.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking to support the plant as it can grow taller than most dwarf-indeterminate releases. Tasmanian Chocolate bears oblate, beefsteak-style fruit in a deep purple-black hue with well-balanced, rich flavor typical of dark-fleshed 'black' tomatoes. It resulted from a 2006 cross of New Big Dwarf and Paul Robeson made by Patrina Nuske Small in Australia, selected and named by Linda Reid of Tasmania, and released through the Dwarf Tomato Project. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for the best flavor.

common_name: Uluru Ochre Tomato (Orange-Green Ruffled Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit suits raised beds and containers, and it is an early, prolific producer among dwarfs.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking lightly since the sturdy stems need less support than sprawling indeterminate types. Uluru Ochre bears ruffled, oblate fruit with orange flesh tinged in green, giving each tomato an amber, earthy appearance that inspired its name after the Australian landmark; the flavor is rich and complex when the plant is at its best. It began as a cross between an orange heirloom and Rosella Purple made by Patrina Nuske Small, stabilized by a team of Dwarf Tomato Project volunteers, and released as an OSSI-pledged variety. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine.

common_name: Sweet Adelaide Tomato (Pink Ruffled Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact, tree-like 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking the sturdy, tree-like stems lightly for support. Sweet Adelaide bears meaty pink fruit ranging from round to boat-shaped with somewhat ruffled shoulders, prized for its excellent, well-balanced sweetness on a compact plant. It descends from a New Big Dwarf x Paul Robeson cross and was named by Patrina Nuske Small, one of many collaborative releases from the Dwarf Tomato Project bred to bring heirloom flavor to small-space gardens. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for the best flavor.

common_name: Loxton Lad Tomato (Orange Beefsteak Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact, tree-type 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit suits raised beds and containers.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking the thick, rugose-leafed stems lightly for support. Loxton Lad bears large, smooth, oblate orange beefsteak fruit with well-balanced, delicious flavor, notably bigger than its sibling release Loxton Lass. It originated from a 2009 Rosella Purple x orange heirloom cross made by Patrina Nuske Small, stabilized over several seasons by Dwarf Tomato Project volunteers, and released as an OSSI-pledged variety. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for peak sweetness.

common_name: Dwarf Golden Gypsy Tomato (Yellow Potato-Leaf Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact, tree-like 2-4 ft dwarf-indeterminate habit with potato-leaf foliage suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking the sturdy, potato-leaf stems lightly for support. Dwarf Golden Gypsy bears medium to large oblate yellow fruit with pale yellow flesh and an intense, sprightly, refreshingly tangy flavor rated among the best of the newer dwarf releases. It began as a Golden Dwarf Champion x Elbe cross made by Patrina Nuske Small, was selected and renamed by Wendy Montanez, and stabilized over multiple generations by Dwarf Tomato Project volunteers before its 2015 release as an OSSI-pledged variety. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for best flavor.

common_name: Dwarf Arctic Rose Tomato (Early Pink Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; the compact 2-3 ft dwarf habit and unusually early maturity suit raised beds, containers, and short-season gardens.

directions: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost into fertile, well-drained soil, staking lightly since the thick, rugose-leafed stems need less support than sprawling indeterminate types. Dwarf Arctic Rose bears round to oblate pink fruit with smooth shoulders and clear skin over red flesh, offering well-balanced flavor on one of the earliest-maturing plants in the Dwarf Tomato Project lineup, sometimes ready weeks ahead of other dwarf releases. It was bred from a 2005 cross of Budai Torpe and Black from Tula made by Patrina Nuske Small, with selection work carried out largely by Alaska-based growers well-suited to short seasons. Harvest as fruit ripens fully on the vine for the best flavor.
